transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Laura Gomez (Orion Head of Data), Mark Rivera (CTO), Sana Patel (Compliance), Jin Wu (ML Engineer)

Summary: quick scoping call to nail down POC data handling requirements and benchmark plan. Focused on PII handling, redaction vs tokenization, logging levels, retention windows, and where prompts are stored.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this focused. Ethan and I are from Redwood, thanks for making time. Can folks say quick intro?
[00:12] Laura Gomez: Hi, Laura here, head of data at Orion Health. We're running a patient messaging workflow that we'd like to pilot with Redwood to improve triage responses.
[00:20] Mark Rivera: Mark, CTO. Primary concerns are PHI handling and latency for real-time triage, also cost.
[00:27] Sana Patel: Sana, compliance. Need to understand data residency, audit logs, KMS and redaction options.
[00:33] Jin Wu: Jin, ML engineer, I'll run the benchmarks and integrate the SDK.
[00:38] Ethan Park: Great; quick agenda: success criteria, data handling (PII/redaction/logging), workload sizing for benchmarks, timeline and next steps.

[00:46] Maya Chen: To start, what's the success criteria for this pilot from your side? Latency targets? throughput? quality?
[00:53] Mark Rivera: Latency target is 500ms p95 for 1-2 concurrent requests per user across our clinics. For throughput, think 300 requests per minute during peak. Quality: match or exceed current rule-based accuracy on entity extraction and triage label correctness by 10%.
[01:12] Laura Gomez: And we need to ensure no PHI leaks into logs or third-party storage. Ideally, PII is redacted before payload leaves our VPC. If that's not possible, we need encrypted storage with KMS and short retention.
[01:28] Ethan Park: Understood. For PII we have a few options: client-side redaction before send, server-side automated redaction using regex and NER, or using a dedicated private deployment where data never touches shared storage. All have tradeoffs.
[01:44] Sana Patel: Can you outline the differences? Particularly around auditability — we need proof of what was stored and for how long.
[01:51] Ethan Park: Sure. Client-side redaction means you remove PHI fields in your app; nothing Redwood receives is PHI. Best for compliance but increases integration work and might affect model outputs if you remove context. Server-side redaction can mask or replace PII at ingestion; we can provide redaction rules and an option to retain only hashed tokens for reruns. Private deployments (Redwood Private) ensure data stays in your VPC or on-prem; logs and prompt storage can be configured to your KMS and retention policy.
[02:18] Maya Chen: Important note — for the hosted API we do have options to disable persistent prompt storage and to limit access to transcripts, but by default we retain short-term logs for debugging unless you opt out or choose Private. That's often a sticking point.
[02:31] Laura Gomez: When you say "disable persistent prompt storage" does that mean you still temporarily cache prompts? And for how long? Our lawyers ask about even transient storage.
[02:39] Ethan Park: Right now our runtime uses in-memory KV cache for performance; ephemeral caching during the request lifecycle is unavoidable. For hosted customers we keep short debug logs for up to 24 hours by default, but we can configure a zero-retention plan for a POC if needed, or route logs to customer-controlled s3 with provided KMS keys — that depends on the deployment.
[02:57] Mark Rivera: So for a POC we could do hosted with log forwarding to our S3 and a short retention, or do a private deployment if we want absolute control. What's the timeline delta and cost delta?
[03:09] Ethan Park: Private deployment is heavier — setup and network peering, maybe 2-4 weeks to stand up depending on your infra and approvals. There's also a platform fee. Hosted with log forwarding and a zero-retention debugging window we can do faster — usually pilot-ready within a week if credentials and sample data are provided. For benchmarking fidelity, both approaches work; private gives you the cleanest compliance story.
[03:33] Sana Patel: For SOC2 evidence, we need access to audit logs showing who accessed what and when. Can you export audit logs to our SIEM?
[03:40] Maya Chen: Yes, we can ship audit logs via syslog or cloudtrail style exports to your SIEM, and tie to SSO/SAML IDs. We'll include the AUDIT export runbook in the security pack.
[03:49] Jin Wu: On prompt storage: if we disable persistent storage will that impact our ability to reproduce responses for evaluation? We need to run offline evaluations and debug edge cases.
[03:58] Ethan Park: Good point. If persistent prompt storage is disabled, you can still send duplicates of the payloads to your own bucket for evaluation, or we can do ephemeral recording for X hours and then purge after you retrieve them. For reproducibility we recommend hashed identifiers mapped to your stored payloads in your S3 so you can rehydrate requests without us storing raw prompts.
[04:19] Laura Gomez: That sounds workable. For PII mapping, our team will produce a sample that highlights typical PHI elements: name, MRN, DOB, address, small notes. We'll annotate which fields must be stripped vs hashed.
[04:31] Maya Chen: Great. On logging and metrics, we can expose per-route token-level cost, latency histograms, and per-token logs masked by default. For the POC we'll enable detailed metrics and mask PII tokens. But we need agreement on what masking looks like (e.g., <NAME>, <MRN>) so the ML team can still use context for debugging.
[04:53] Mark Rivera: What's the benchmark plan look like? Jin, what do you plan to run?
[05:00] Jin Wu: We'll run a synthetic workload that mirrors production: 70% short triage messages (<100 tokens), 30% long summaries (~400 tokens). We'll instruments p95 latency, average tokens per request, success rate of correct triage label, and hallucination rate on extracted entities. Ideally run 10k requests across different concurrency windows.
[05:22] Ethan Park: Perfect. For sizing we'll need the sample distributions and Jin's load script; we can provide a k6 based benchmark harness and a config that hits the model endpoints under different batch and quantization profiles. For the POC we usually run three model variants: a base open model, a quantized variant, and a latency-optimized variant to compare cost/perf.
[05:43] Laura Gomez: Cost is big. We'll need estimates: tokens per request, expected QPS, and a cost model. Can Redwood provide a preliminary cost-by-variant spreadsheet?
[05:52] Maya Chen: Yes, Ethan will produce a cost estimate after we see your sample distribution. We'll also recommend batching and KV cache settings to hit your p95 target without overspending.
[06:03] Sana Patel: About retention — legally we can keep patient data for analytics but with strict controls. For the pilot we prefer 7-day retention of raw prompts, and 90 days for aggregated metrics. Is 7 days doable?
[06:13] Ethan Park: For hosted, we can configure debug logs to 24 hours by default; for 7 days we'd likely forward logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules. Private deployment can natively support 7-day retention in our audit config. For the POC a compromise is: host with forwarding and your S3 lifecycle set to 7 days.
[06:28] Mark Rivera: Who has the encryption keys in that setup?
[06:31] Maya Chen: We can support customer-managed keys (CMK) in most cloud deployments. If logs are forwarded to your S3, you hold the keys; if you choose Private, you can bring your HSM/KMS.
[06:40] Laura Gomez: We need to see the network diagram and what ports/hardening is required for log forwarding and for the model endpoints.
[06:46] Maya Chen: We'll include a network architecture diagram in the security pack.
[06:50] Ethan Park: Back to success criteria — to recap your targets: p95 latency <= 500ms, throughput up to 300 rpm peak, and quality improvement of +10% on triage accuracy. For security: zero-long-term-PHI retention or 7-day retention on customer S3. Does that capture it?
[07:07] Laura Gomez: Yes. Also we need audit exports to SIEM and SSO integration.
[07:12] Sana Patel: And SOC2/ISO docs before we sign any pilot contract.
[07:15] Maya Chen: We'll send the SOC2 pack and ISO summary along with the network diagram and the benchmark harness.
[07:21] Jin Wu: For the benchmark harness, can you provide example configs for batching and quantization options? We want to test int8 quantized vs float16 with different batch sizes.
[07:30] Ethan Park: Absolutely — we'll supply runnable configs and recommended kernel params. Note that quantization can speed up throughput but may affect entity extraction quality; that's why we test multiple profiles.
[07:42] Mark Rivera: Timeline question: if we get sample data by 2025-11-27, when can we expect pilot kickoff?
[07:49] Maya Chen: If we have data and IAM access by 11/27, we can kickoff the week of 12/1. Benchmark runs and initial results usually take 1-2 weeks, then a short tuning cycle. Total pilot length: 6 weeks to show data and results.
[08:03] Laura Gomez: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:07] Ethan Park: Main blockers: receiving sample data with PII mapping, confirming whether you'll accept hosted-with-forwarding or require Private, and SSO/SAML details for audit.
[08:17] Maya Chen: We'll attach the security pack and the benchmark template right after this call. Expect an email with links and the next steps.
[08:24] Laura Gomez: Thanks. One last thing — can you confirm what "masking" looks like in logs? We want placeholders but still need token counts and sequence context for debugging.
[08:34] Ethan Park: We'll mask strings with consistent tokens like <NAME>, <MRN>, keep token counts intact, and provide a hashed reference id that maps to your S3 object if you choose to store the raw prompt. That way you can rehydrate locally for debug.
[08:46] Sana Patel: That mapping needs to be auditable and we want the hashes logged as well.
[08:50] Maya Chen: Noted — we'll include hashing scheme details and audit log examples in the security pack.
[08:57] Maya Chen: Okay let's recap next steps.
[09:00] Maya Chen: (1) Redwood to send SOC2/ISO + network diagram + benchmark harness (Ethan & Maya) by 2025-11-21/22.
[09:09] Maya Chen: (2) Orion to provide sample dataset (50-100 de-identified conversations) and PII mapping by 2025-11-27.
[09:15] Maya Chen: (3) Schedule pilot kickoff week of 2025-12-01.
[09:18] Maya Chen: Any other questions?
[09:20] Mark Rivera: No, good meeting.
[09:22] Laura Gomez: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
